chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem ibn Ibrahim, from Abbad ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his mature son to an orphan girl in his custody. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She inherits him if he dies, and he does not inherit her, because she has the choice (to annul the marriage), and there is no choice against her.'

key_terms.وَلَا خِيَارَ عَلَيْهَا: and there is no choice against her

ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit her husband if they were married by his father while she was still a minor?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the asymmetrical inheritance rights in a marriage where the wife is a minor under the husband's guardianship, establishing that she inherits him while he does not inherit her. The ruling hinges on the concept of 'al-khiyar' (option), where the minor wife retains the right to annul the marriage upon maturity, whereas the husband, being 'mudrak' (mature/capable), does not possess a reciprocal right of annulment against her. This distinction underscores the protective legal status of the minor spouse in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts and subsequent inheritance distribution.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Naeem Bin Ibrahim, from Abbad Bin Kaseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who got his mature son married to an orphan girls in his custody. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would inherit him if he dies, and he would not inherit her because for her there is the choice (to get married again), and there is no choice against her’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Nu’aym ibn Ibrahim from ‘Abbad ibn Kathir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who arranges marriage for his mature son with an orphan girl in his custody. He (the Imam) said, ‘She will inherit him if he dies because she has the choice to approve or disapprove the marriage after she becomes mature and there is no choice against her.’”
